LESSON: AUDITORY DISCRIMINATION

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: LISTENING
Topic 1.5: Auditory discrimination

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Auditory discrimination. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Respond appropriately to sounds in the environment.
2. Enjoy listening to sounds in the environment. sounds they hear. voice recognition activities. identifying various sounds in the environment. audio clips. Core-competence developed: Learning to learn, digital literacy

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Respond appropriately to sounds in the environment.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to respond appropriately to sounds in the environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. Enjoy listening to sounds in the environment. sounds they hear. voice recognition activities. identifying various sounds in the environment. audio clips. Core-competence developed: Learning to learn, digital literacy
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to enjoy listening to sounds in the environment. sounds they hear. voice recognition activities. identifying various sounds in the environment. audio clips. Core-competence developed: Learning to learn, digital literacy. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Auditory discrimination.
2. Explain Auditory discrimination to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Auditory discrimination.
4. Show that you can: Respond appropriately to sounds in the environment.
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Auditory discrimination. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Auditory discrimination important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. Respond appropriately to sounds in the environment.
2. Enjoy listening to sounds in the environment. sounds they hear. voice recognition activities. identifying various sounds in the environment. audio clips. Core-competence developed: Learning to learn, digital literacy

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
